name: Microsoft Skelton Grange datacentre campus, Leeds
summary: Planned Microsoft hyperscale datacentre campus on the former Skelton Grange power station land at Stourton, Leeds, beside the River Aire. Microsoft bought the first 27-acre plot from Harworth Group in 2024, and a second 21-acre plot is due to transfer. The application covers three data centre buildings of about 424,000 sq ft (about 500,000 sq ft with auxiliary buildings) plus power, water and energy infrastructure. Leeds planners resolved to grant consent in April 2026, subject to conditions and a Section 106 agreement. Harworth estimates about GBP 4 billion of inward investment at completion; a start on site was expected within 12 to 18 months.

Microsoft held a two-day public consultation on 11-12 June 2025 while preparing its planning application (later registered as 25/06139/FU).
Leeds City Council planners resolved to grant the hybrid application, delegating final approval to the Chief Planning Officer subject to conditions and a Section 106 agreement.
Construction Enquirer reported a start on site was likely within 12 to 18 months of the April 2026 approval.

notes: No power capacity figure for the campus was found in the cited sources; Harworth's 0.8 GW figure refers to its wider powered-land portfolio, not this campus. Harworth's release footnote dates the plans panel to 23/04/2027, apparently a typo for 2026. The Construction Index page shows only day and month; the year is taken from its context alongside the same-day Harworth release.
